summary: Intro discovery to understand Apogee's inference needs: heavy multi-lingual support, long-context (20k-40k) for legal documents, tool-calling for downstream systems, and regulatory constraints. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs, benchmarking plan, and next steps for security docs and pilot.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-11 16:00-17:02 UTC | Duration ~62m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Liu (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Evan (Apogee Head of ML), Sana (Platform Eng), Jon (Security), Lucia (PM)

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros then we'll jump into what you need from an inference standpoint.
00:09 Evan: Hi, thanks. I'm Evan. We're evaluating options for serving a few LLM-powered features across our product lines, mostly legal doc summarization and bilingual customer support.
00:18 Maya: Great. Connor and Liu on the call to go deep on latency/cost and deployment options. Sana, are you the infra contact?
00:24 Sana: Yup that's me. We'll probably be the ones coordinating networking and VPC setup.
00:28 Connor: Awesome. Quick qual question: expected QPS for synchronous generation and typical prompt lengths?
00:35 Evan: For the legal flow, it's mostly 10-20 requests per minute per user but the payloads are large — average document is 10-30k tokens, sometimes up to 40k. We also want to support Spanish and Japanese outputs.
00:46 Liu: Okay so this is long-context—32k+ model compat, or segmentation with retrieval. Are you currently using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)?
00:55 Lucia: We're experimenting with RAG but the legal team wants the full context preserved in the prompt for traceability, so we'd prefer native long context when possible.
01:04 Connor: That pushes us toward model variants that support 32k-65k contexts or doing smart chunking plus KV cache and prefix caching. Hosted options can run larger models but we need to size for memory and latency.
01:15 Jon: Security wise: we've got to keep data residency requirements, SSO/SAML for admin console, and KMS for key management. Also audit logs retention for 7 years. Can Redwood handle that in Dedicated or Private?
01:26 Maya: Yes. For Dedicated you get customer-isolated GPU pools and can integrate with your KMS. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives full control including HSM options. We'll send the security playbook.
01:36 Sana: Latency target is <800ms for short chat queries, but for the legal summarization higher latency is acceptable as long as throughput is predictable. Cost is also a constraint — we want to optimize token cost.
01:48 Connor: There's always a trade-off — bigger context models cost more per token and have higher latency. We can propose a mixed routing policy: smaller, quantized models for chat, and larger context models for batch summarize jobs with a routing fallback.
02:01 Lucia: Tool-calling — we need a way for the model to call internal services (document metadata fetch, citation verifier). Does Redwood support function/tool calling with structured outputs?
02:10 Liu: Yes, we support tool-calling and structured responses. Function calling goes through a secure invocation layer; you can restrict which tools models can call and log the calls for audit.
02:20 Evan: Any limitations on tool calling in Private mode?
02:24 Connor: In Private mode you control the network egress and ingress, so tool endpoints can be inside your VPC. We provide the function-calling hook and instrument the calls for traceability, but the actual invocation endpoints are customer-managed when on-prem/VPC.
02:37 Jon: Regarding compliance: SOC2 attestation, ISO? We need to see the certs. Also curious about data retention and purge controls.
02:45 Maya: We'll attach SOC2 and the data retention policy. On dedicated we can set log retention policies and purge hooks; on Private it's fully customer-controlled.
02:55 Evan: Model selection — we want open models where possible. Which open models do you recommend for 32k context + multi-lingual?
03:03 Connor: A few candidates: long-context LLaMA derivatives with 32k windows, Mistral variants for 32k recently, and some specialized long-context models like Mixtral/LongT5-type. There's also quantized LLMs that keep performance but lower memory. We'll map by accuracy on English/Spanish/Japanese tests.
03:18 Lucia: Any concerns about hallucinations with long-context? We need citations and provenance.
03:23 Liu: Yes, hallucination risk increases. For legal we recommend deterministic decoding, chain-of-thought suppression, and citing retrieved passages. We'll instrument a citation layer with tool-calling to fetch original paragraphs.
03:36 Sana: For benchmarks, can we run a 1-week dedicated test with our dataset? We'll need scriptability to replay requests and measure latency, p50/p95, and token cost.
03:45 Connor: Absolutely. We'll prepare a benchmark harness. Ideally we run an initial hosted benchmark for quick comparison, then dedicated for production-like numbers. For the 32k flows we likely need dedicated GPUs unless using special quantization.
03:57 Evan: What's the typical cost delta hosted vs dedicated vs private? Ballpark numbers are fine now.
04:02 Maya: Hosted is easiest but highest per-token cost. Dedicated brings unit cost down via reserved capacity; Private has higher upfront but best for compliance and predictable long-term cost. We'll share a sample pricing matrix.
04:12 Jon: Networking — can Redwood integrate with our centralized logging and SIEM?
04:16 Priya: Yes, we can forward audit logs, tracing and event hooks to your SIEM; for Private we can ship logs directly into your collectors.
04:24 Lucia: Multilingual evaluation — we want to test Spanish legalese and Japanese contracts. Any sandbox models tuned for multilingual legal?
04:31 Connor: There are some open models fine-tuned for multilingual but legal domain fine-tuning will help. We recommend a small-domain fine-tune or instruction-tuning on your corpora for the highest accuracy. We'll include fine-tune vs prompt engineering tradeoffs in the POC plan.
04:47 Evan: Timeframe: we want a POC within 3 weeks and a decision in 2 months. Is that reasonable?
04:53 Maya: Yes that's doable. Immediate next: send security docs, pricing, and proposed POC plan. Then baseline benchmarks and schedule deep technical session.
05:01 Jon: One more question — model version pinning and rollbacks. We need deterministic rollbacks for auditability.
05:07 Liu: Redwood supports model version pinning and fast rollbacks; we also have canary rollouts and A/B tests with automatic fallback policies.
05:15 Lucia: Great. Any blockers for starting a hosted POC now?
05:18 Sana: We can start with hosted for fast iteration; network & compliance won't block an initial evaluation.
05:25 Maya: Perfect. We'll send the pack. Thanks everyone.
05:30 Evan: Thanks, appreciate it.

End of transcript.

Shared artifacts mentioned: Apogee POC deck (link: https://redwood-internal.example/sales/apogee-deck), benchmark template (https://redwood-internal.example/benchmarks/apogee-template), security pack (will be attached in follow-up).

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-attribution, some technical terms misspelled (KV cache -> K-V cache, HSM as H-M-S), filler words present.
